newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WEEK AHEAD - Rate cut talk to drive Australian mkts.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Rate cut talk to drive Australian mkts.

text.p: The Australian data landscape is fairly barren this week, but that is not expected to stop speculation of a rate cut from being the dominant force on local markets.

"With nothing much else on the domestic agenda next week, local markets will have an opportunity to digest the implications of events of the past few weeks," Commonwealth Bank economist Tim Moloney said.

And with most of those events -- including retail trade, labour force, consumer and business sentiment data -- showing some softness after a strong start to the year, talk of a fifth rate cut has increased.
Economists now see a 60 percent chance of a rate cut, compared with 35 percent just two weeks ago.

"There will be much debate about whether or not a move will occur, whether it would achieve much and whether it would send the Australian dollar into a tailspin," Colonial State Bank group economist Hans Kunnen said.
With the continuing high unemployment rate seen as one of voters major concerns, the fact that economists see no improvement by year end is expected to keep the pressure up for lower rates.
"While the prospects of one more cut are finely balanced, right now, we think the odds favour another show of support for the unemployed from the RBA," ANZ economists said in a report.
Employment is only expected to grow by 15,000 a month in the second half of 1997, a rate seen only consistent with stopping unemployment from rising. Unemployment is seen at 8.6 percent by year end.

U.S. data will also be important this week -- anything that follows on from Friday's U.S. PPI data in pointing to U.S. rates being on hold at the July 1 and 2 FOMC meeting will see expectations raised of the possibility of a local rate cut.
The PPI fell 0.3 percent in May, the first time in 45 years the series has fallen in five successive months, suggesting U.S. inflation pressures remained well contained.
While the Reserve Bank of Australia board next meets on July 1, the RBA can cut on any day it chooses, which means traders will be closely watching their screens at 9.30 a.m. each day.
Apart from some secondary pieces of data, the only figure economists forecast this week is first quarter dwelling commencements due out on Tuesday.

Given signs of a housing sector recovery, and the strength in approvals and finance data round the end of 1996 and 1997, a second consecutive rise in this series is expected, but it is not seen having any impact on markets.
AUSTRALIAN BONDS (Fri: 10 yr cash yield 7.02 pct, 3-yr 5.80)

Australian 10-year bond yields look set to open the week below 7.0 percent for the first time since February 1994, given the break of 93.010 resistance in Friday's SYCOM session on data showing U.S. inflation pressures remain moderate.

Those figures added to the growing doubts the U.S. will lift rates after the July 1/2 FOMC meeting, and boosted a local market that is on red alert for a rate cut this week after the recent run of data showed that the Reserve Bank and the government will be struggling to make their growth aspirations.
This has seen spreads contract markedly, with the spread to 10 years Treasuries falling to 50 basis points last week.

"With a paucity of domestic data, the key influences on domestic interest rate markets will be speculation on the timing of the next move in monetary policy and the run of U.S. data," Societe Generale economist Glenn Maguire said.
However, the early part of Monday's session is likely to be volatile as three and 10-year bond futures contracts roll over to September from June ahead of the midday close-out.
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri: US$0.7524/29, New York US$0.7516/21)
While talk of a rate cut is underpinning a bullish credit market, it is weighing heavily on the Australian dollar.

From six year highs of US$0.8200 in early December ahead of the third rate cut, the dollar fell to 16 month lows of just above US$0.7500 last week, and analysts felt it could test lower as speculation mounted of another rate cut.

"The Australian dollar could, in the immediate future, fall to the lower end of our current 'fair value' range of US$0.74-79 in reaction to a perceived erosion of relative interest rate support," Macquarie Bank economists said.
With little local data this week, the ongoing rate cut speculation is expected to cap any rallies, with a test of support at US$0.7450 seen as more likely than an upside test.
STOCKS (Fri: All Ordinaries 2,655.3, up 2.1 pct)
Another quiet week in terms of expected corporate releases should keep investor focused on offshore markets and on individual share plays or rumours.

The market is expected to build on the record close to last week after the U.S. market continued to power ahead on Friday. The Dow industrials posted its sixth successive record close when it ended up 70.57 points, or 0.92 percent, at 7782.04.

Cyclical sectors like manufacturing and transport are seen swayed more than other sectors by any volatility on Wall Street. Diversified manufacturer, Pacific Dunlop Ltd and transport group, Brambles Industries Ltd were two of the obvious benefactors of the Dow's strong showing last week.
Technical analysts noted the key Fibonacci retracement level for the All Ordinaries index at 2650 was breached on Friday, technically speaking a bullish sign for the short term.
But dealers warned Australian investors have been reluctant to run with Wall Street strength in recent years and were particularly cautious when the Dow's run was almost unbroken.

"I'm suprised Wall Street hasn't had more down days lately. It will make local investors more cautious - too many people remember October 1987," said Grant Williams, a dealer at Sydney broker, Reynolds & Co.
Food company Burns Philp should remain closely watched after a mystery buyer snared a 14.7 percent stake before the start of trade on Friday.
Investors were seen keen to sell into Burns Philp's rally on Friday with dealers suggesting any bid for the company would not be too far from the mystery buyer's price of A$2.50.

The bank sector should also continue to have fascination, especially after Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd's rapid rise last Thursday on recycled rumours a foreign bank was about to launch a takeover offer.
The market will also be looking for any late adjustment to analysts' forecasts for the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's final profit to be announced at the end of the June.
One planned corporate event is the share market debut of Adelaide Marine Ltd this Thursady after its issue of 80 million shares at A$2.00 each.
